note: The fuzz harness passes the raw input bytes and their length directly to the PAC parser.
The first four input bytes control the PAC buffer count; the PoC sets this field to 0x10000000.
The buffer count is multiplied by the 16-byte table entry size and added to the 8-byte header without checking for integer overflow.
After 32-bit wraparound, header_len is small enough for the tiny PoC to pass the bounds check.
The same unchecked count is used to size the in-memory buffer descriptor array, allowing an undersized allocation when the expression wraps.
The parser iterates according to the huge untrusted count even though the accepted input contains only a tiny descriptor table.
With the 5120-byte PoC, the huge loop consumes the supplied descriptor bytes and then reads the next descriptor offset from poisoned bytes beyond the raw fuzz input.
